correctness.rationale: For all positive factors, product length is the sum of lengths minus one. Any divisor is a positive integer not exceeding its digitwise-maximum sum. For n>=b a same-length candidate with units digit toggled to zero or one lies in the interval up to the sum and cannot factor n, because the cofactor must have one digit and then preserves that candidate units digit. One-digit factorization gives equality only for n=1. The finite checker corroborates all 1019 tested n across bases 2..10.
